reference_action: Dense wet medium/overwatering; repot into a chunkier draining mix and reduce watering, then allow recovery. OP reports new leaves after repotting from overwatering and time.

sources.reason: Explicitly replace soggy dense soil with a chunky mix; this is the validated central action despite distracting flower removal and peroxide advice.
Explicitly recommends chunky soil that does not stay wet and reducing watering; hydro conversions and other alternatives are extra.
General Goldilocks watering and medium discussion, with a future LECA reset promised, does not actually instruct this soil repotting or reduced-watering remedy.
Consistent moisture and winter dormancy watering reduction do not address this dense-soil overwatering case; no corrective repot.
Focuses on drying out roots and conversion to self-watering pon; does not recover the validated soil repot and reduced watering.

actions.action: Repot in less dense chunky mix

resolved.reason: Soggy soil and chunky replacement are explicit among alternative diagnoses. Unspecified peroxide bath and unnecessary flower removal add risk/ambiguity, but likely severe harm is not established without a stated concentration or compulsory destructive step.

harmfulness.reason: “Peroxide bath” lacks dilution and duration, so safe implementation is uncertain. Root pruning is limited to dead or rotten roots, but cutting flowers is presented without establishing it is needed.

specificity_accuracy.reason: “Soil looks soggy” and a “chunky soil” replacement fit the reference. Flower-energy and light-stress explanations distract from the supported wet-medium problem, and the suggestions do not converge on one plan.

feasibility.reason: Checking roots and changing the mix are understandable. Several alternative media and an unspecified peroxide bath require additional decisions and purchases.
